content:
Recent public perception of Meta AI glasses has been notably poor—so poor that, as of today, one of the top three spots on the U.S. iPhone paid App Store chart is occupied by an app specifically designed to detect who nearby might be wearing smart glasses.

The app's name leaves little to the imagination: Antizuck Smart Glasses Scanner, which claims to detect and alert you when someone nearby is wearing Meta AI glasses.

Enough iPhone users are willing to spend US$3 to try out this app that it currently ranks No. 3 on the U.S. iPhone paid App Store chart—a rare feat for a newly launched paid app.

We have not tested the app ourselves and cannot confirm whether it actually works; moreover, even if it can detect AI glasses, what you should do once you spot someone wearing them remains unclear.

Smart glasses equipped with cameras are still fairly easy to spot these days, so you probably don't need an app to notice who is wearing them.

Still, people's attitude is crystal clear: many are quite turned off by the concept of AI smart glasses, seeing them as a privacy issue. If Apple wants to join the smart glasses fray next year, this represents a considerable headwind.
